=== F5 (NEW, BLOCKING, REPRODUCED). THE EXEMPTION COVERS THE FILES THAT DEFINE THE GATES, NOT JUST BOOKKEEPING. ===
The PR body says the change "only exempts pure bookkeeping commits under `reviews/`/`proof/`". That is not what `_is_record_only_commit` accepts. It accepts ANY path under `reviews/` or `proof/` -- which includes reviews/schema.json, proof/schema.json and proof/exempt.json. Those are not bookkeeping: reviews/schema.json is loaded and enforced by `_validate_against_schema`, and proof/exempt.json is the named-gap list `lwb_check_proof.py` reads at EXEMPT_PATH to decide which merges may land with no proof record at all.
REPRODUCTION, on a scratch clone at this head, author `Probe Impostor <impostor@example.com>`:
  1. Edited reviews/schema.json alone, setting `required` to []. Committed. That commit touches nothing else.
  2. `_is_record_only_commit(HEAD)` -> True.
  3. python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base feab6ef --head HEAD -> "lwb-commit-identity check passed", EXIT 0.
  4. A/B against the base, with main's copies of BOTH scripts dropped into the same working tree so REPO_ROOT resolves identically: the SAME commit -> "FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: Probe Impostor <impostor@example.com>", EXIT 1. Restoring this branch's copies -> passes again. So this PR is what changes the answer.
  5. `resolve_reviewable_head('feab6ef..HEAD')` -> 4793afcc, i.e. it skips the schema-gutting commit, so no review record has to name it either.
  6. And the gutted schema is genuinely load-bearing, not decorative: `_validate_against_schema({'pr':99,'verdict':'AGREE'}, ...)` returns 5 errors against the intact schema and 0 against the gutted one.
Net: after this PR, a commit under ANY author identity can rewrite the schema the review gate enforces, and neither lwb-commit-identity nor the reviewable-head calculation will see it. commit-identity was the LAST gate that still looked at record-only commits; this removes it. My predecessor's F6 flagged the proof/ half of this as a docstring wording nit; measured end to end it is more than that.
I am NOT saying the exemption is wrong -- the asymmetry it fixes is real and well argued. I am saying its boundary is `reviews/` and `proof/` when it should be the RECORDS in them. A narrow fix: have the identity check treat only `reviews/<n>/*.json` and `proof/<n>.json` as exempt, leaving schema.json and exempt.json inside the gate.
